## SharedGpuSlot.kt { #sharedgpuslot-kt }

One slot of the GPU memory a diffusion session shares with its worker: a device-local buffer and
a timeline semaphore, both exported to the worker as file descriptors.

A [`StreamDiffusionSession`](video.md#streamdiffusionsession-kt-streamdiffusionsession) allocates a ring of these for the frames it sends and another for the
results it reads back, passes their descriptors over a Unix socket, and afterwards exchanges
only slot indices and semaphore values with the worker. Pixels are written and read by the GPU at
both ends: a slot is a dedicated device-local allocation and is never mapped for the CPU. Its
barrier moves the buffer between Field's graphics queue and the external queue CUDA works on, and
the device UUID it reports names the GPU the worker is to import onto. Construction asks the
driver whether it can export this buffer and this kind of semaphore, and fails rather than
handing over a descriptor the worker cannot use.

## SpinningDiffusionDemo.kt { #spinningdiffusiondemo-kt }

A complete demo: [`SpinningDiffusionDemo`](video.md#spinningdiffusiondemo-kt-spinningdiffusiondemo) draws five rotating curves into a source texture,
runs them through a [`StreamDiffusionView`](video.md#streamdiffusionview-kt-streamdiffusionview), and shows source and stylized output side by side.

It also supplies a renderer-derived motion provider for its ribbons, so it exercises display
reprojection and history blending. Set `angle` to turn the curves.

## SpinningDiffusionMotion.kt { #spinningdiffusionmotion-kt }

The motion provider behind the spinning-curves demo, which derives per-pixel correspondence from
the geometry Field drew rather than from the two images.

[`SpinningDiffusionDemo`](video.md#spinningdiffusiondemo-kt-spinningdiffusiondemo)'s five curves are ribbons carrying a surface id per vertex, and the
rotation that drew each frame is kept against that frame's id. To answer a request this projects
every pixel's surface point back through the reference frame's rotation, which is the position
that point had then; an id pass rendered at the reference angle says whether the surface visible
there is the same one, so a ribbon that has turned behind another is rejected instead of carrying
the wrong colour across. The correspondence ribbon is widened well past the drawn line, so the
broader marks the model returns are covered too, and confidence falls off toward its edge.

The fallback pass covers what the mask rejected. Where the current frame shows bare paper it
fills from paper near that pixel in the reference image, so the rejected band carries no bright
impression of the reference frame's curves into empty paper, and it leaves every pixel the
current source actually drew.

## StreamDiffusionConfig.kt { #streamdiffusionconfig-kt }

Settings for the optional streaming-diffusion backend: where it is installed, the prompt and
strength, the seed, frame rate and the temporal options.

[`StreamDiffusionConfig`](video.md#streamdiffusionconfig-kt-streamdiffusionconfig) validates its ranges on construction and is handed to a
[`StreamDiffusionView`](video.md#streamdiffusionview-kt-streamdiffusionview). [`StreamDiffusionPresets`](video.md#streamdiffusionconfig-kt-streamdiffusionpresets) holds named prompts (ink, charcoal, wire, and white-on-black variants);
change prompt, strength, seed or noise advection on a running view with `view.reset(...)`.

## StreamDiffusionMotion.kt { #streamdiffusionmotion-kt }

The interface a renderer implements to give streaming diffusion per-pixel motion:
[`StreamDiffusionMotionProvider`](video.md#streamdiffusionmotion-kt-streamdiffusionmotionprovider), with the frame and request types it receives.

A provider answers each [`StreamDiffusionMotionRequest`](video.md#streamdiffusionmotion-kt-streamdiffusionmotionrequest) with an RGBA32F texture mapping pixels of
the current frame back to a reference frame, plus confidence and rejection channels. The view
uses it for display reprojection, history blending and noise advection.

### StreamDiffusionMotionProvider { #streamdiffusionmotion-kt-streamdiffusionmotionprovider }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">StreamDiffusionMotionProvider</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/video/diffusion/StreamDiffusionMotion/#L31)

Optional renderer-owned backward correspondence. RGBA32F, same size as the source: RG = absolute normalized UV in reference, B = confidence [0,1], A = reactive rejection [0,1]. UV uses the same orientation as sampling the source RTT; pixel centres are (xy+.5)/extent. Confidence zero means unknown/disoccluded. Reject occluded surfaces using depth/object IDs. Implementations may record a target here, reuse it between requests, or return null for unavailable history. No CPU pixels. The returned target must be sampled and transfer-source capable.

## StreamDiffusionSession.kt { #streamdiffusionsession-kt }

The worker process behind a [`StreamDiffusionView`](video.md#streamdiffusionview-kt-streamdiffusionview): [`StreamDiffusionSession`](video.md#streamdiffusionsession-kt-streamdiffusionsession) starts the
Python worker, shares its rings of GPU buffers and semaphores with it, and exchanges JSON control
messages.

Pixels never pass through the protocol; the messages carry slot indices, semaphore values and
frame ids. `status`, `ready`, `capabilities` and `lastStats` report what the worker last said.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/video/diffusion/StreamDiffusionSession.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/video/diffusion/StreamDiffusionSession/)

## StreamDiffusionSupport.kt { #streamdiffusionsupport-kt }

The preflight check for local streaming diffusion: whether this machine can run it, and a
sentence saying what is missing when it cannot.

`probe` reports the first absent piece, looking at the platform, the renderer, the selected
Vulkan device's external memory and semaphore FD support, an NVIDIA device that can export
buffers and timeline semaphores, the backend root and its Python environment, the Field worker
script, the model files a `diffusion` backend needs, and the native handle-passing helper. It
allocates nothing on the GPU, starts no Python and reads no weights, so box code can call it and
show the reason instead of a view. [`StreamDiffusionView`](video.md#streamdiffusionview-kt-streamdiffusionview) and [`StreamDiffusionSession`](video.md#streamdiffusionsession-kt-streamdiffusionsession) each check
it as they are constructed and fail with the same sentence; CUDA, the Python packages, the
weights and TensorRT are checked later, when the worker starts.

`configuredRoot` is where the installation path comes from: `FIELD_STREAMDIFFUSION_ROOT`, or the
one line in `~/.afield/streamdiffusion-root.txt`, which is read on every call so a Field that is
already running finds a backend installed after it started.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/video/diffusion/StreamDiffusionSupport.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/video/diffusion/StreamDiffusionSupport/)

## StreamDiffusionTemporalOutput.kt { #streamdiffusiontemporaloutput-kt }

The temporal half of a diffusion view: it holds the last two results the worker returned and
renders the texture the view publishes.

Results arrive late and in groups, so geometry has moved on by the time a frame can be shown.
Given a [`StreamDiffusionMotionProvider`](video.md#streamdiffusionmotion-kt-streamdiffusionmotionprovider), a [`StreamDiffusionView`](video.md#streamdiffusionview-kt-streamdiffusionview) routes its output through this
file to settle both ends of that delay; without one it publishes the worker's output directly.
Each arriving result is written into one of two history targets while the other is read, blended
with the previous result where the provider's correspondence agrees and both came from the same
worker generation, and the carried colours are clamped to the 3x3 neighbourhood of the fresh ones
so a stroke that moved does not trail. The display target reprojects the newest history onto the
current frame and mixes it with the live source where confidence runs out; with no correspondence
for the current frame it shows that history as it stands.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/video/diffusion/StreamDiffusionTemporalOutput.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/video/diffusion/StreamDiffusionTemporalOutput/)

## StreamDiffusionView.kt { #streamdiffusionview-kt }

A render target that sends a source [`RenderToTexture`](graphics.md#rendertotexture-kt-rendertotexture) through the streaming-diffusion worker
and returns the result as an ordinary sampled texture, [`StreamDiffusionView.output`](video.md#streamdiffusionview-kt--streamdiffusionview--output).

The frames stay on the GPU throughout: the source is copied into shared buffers, the CUDA worker
writes its result into others, and the view copies that back into `output`. Construct and close
a view between frames. With `renderSource = true` the view schedules the source itself; with
`false` the caller renders the source earlier in the same command buffer. An optional
[`StreamDiffusionMotionProvider`](video.md#streamdiffusionmotion-kt-streamdiffusionmotionprovider) enables display reprojection and history blending.

## particleflow.kt { #particleflow-kt }

Tracked particles from a video, turned into a velocity field that can be measured.

[`ParticleVideo`](video.md#particlevideo-kt-particlevideo) follows thousands of points through a movie and leaves a cloud of samples per
frame. This file splats those velocities onto a regular grid, one [`FlowFrame`](video.md#particleflow-kt-flowframe) per frame, so every
cell carries a velocity whether or not a particle landed in it. [`ParticleFlow.at`](video.md#particleflow-kt--particleflow--at) hands one frame
back as an [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img), u in channel 0 and v in channel 1, which is the form the vector-field topology
and streamline code reads.

A tracked video's flow often describes the camera more than its subject, and on old film the
whole frame shifts and turns a little from one frame to the next. So each frame also carries the
camera motion measured from its own particles: a median shift, and an affine fit that picks up a
slight zoom or rotation as well. [`CameraMotion`](video.md#particleflow-kt-cameramotion) chooses how much of that to subtract when a frame
is read back. A flow is far smaller than the tracks it came from, and smaller again gzipped and
quantised, so [`ParticleFlow.save`](video.md#particleflow-kt--particleflow--save) and [`loadParticleFlow`](video.md#particleflow-kt--loadparticleflow) let a page or a test begin from a saved
flow instead of running the tracker.

### CameraMotion { #particleflow-kt-cameramotion }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">CameraMotion</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/video/particleflow/#L37)

What to take out of a flow before using it: nothing (`KEEP`), the frame's median velocity (`SHIFT`), or an affine motion fitted to every particle and refitted without the outliers (`AFFINE`), which also removes a camera's slight zoom and rotation, or old film weaving in the gate.

Constants: `KEEP`, `SHIFT`, `AFFINE`.

### FlowFrame { #particleflow-kt-flowframe }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FlowFrame</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">u</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">v</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">w</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">shift</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">affine</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/video/particleflow/#L45)

One frame of a [`ParticleFlow`](video.md#particleflow-kt-particleflow): the particle velocities splatted onto the grid (weighted sums `u`, `v` and total weight `w` per cell), and the camera motion measured from the particles, as a median `shift` (vx, vy) and an `affine` fit (vx = a0 + a1 x + a2 y, vy = b0 + b1 x + b2 y, in processed-image pixels).

## particletracker.kt { #particletracker-kt }

Runs the optional offline particle tracker (RAFT optical flow, via PyTorch) over a video and
caches the result as a PVTRACK1 file.

[`particleTracker`](video.md#particletracker-kt--particletracker) makes a [`ParticleTracker`](video.md#particletracker-kt-particletracker) for the tools in `optional/particle-tracker`; its
`track` call is a suspend function meant for a box's `start { ... }` coroutine, and it returns a
[`ParticleTrackingRun`](video.md#particletracker-kt-particletrackingrun) whose `load` hands the file to `particlevideo.kt`.
[`ParticleTrackingOptions`](video.md#particletracker-kt-particletrackingoptions) holds every algorithm setting, and each one is part of the cache key.
Invalid options fail before any process starts (`ParticleVideoTest`).

### ParticleTracker { #particletracker-kt-particletracker }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">ParticleTracker</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">tools</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Path</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">python</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cache</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Path</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/video/particletracker/#L121)

Cached offline video processing, intended to be called inside a box's `start { ... }` coroutine. The suspend call owns the Python process: cancellation terminates the wrapper and its inference descendants. Successful runs publish a checksum-validated receipt atomically; failures never become cache hits. Locks share concurrent identical requests across boxes and worktrees.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="particletracker-kt--particletracker--track"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">suspend</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">track</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">input</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">options</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ParticleTrackingOptions</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">ParticleTrackingOptions</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">offline</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">force</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ParticleTrackingRun</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/video/particletracker/#L127) | Tracks a local video, or returns the identical cached run. `offline` refuses a missing pretrained checkpoint without downloading it. `force` recomputes this key while preserving an existing successful result if inference fails. Logs and provenance are retained in the cache. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">suspend</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">track</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">input</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Path</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">options</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ParticleTrackingOptions</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">ParticleTrackingOptions</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">offline</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">force</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ParticleTrackingRun</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/media/video/particletracker/#L132) | Path overload of [`track`](video.md#particletracker-kt--particletracker--track). No shell expansion or string-command interpolation is used. |

## particlevideo.kt { #particlevideo-kt }

Reads particle-tracking results (PVTRACK1 files) as scrubbable frames and per-identity tracks,
with no Python or Torch at load time.

[`loadParticleVideo`](video.md#particlevideo-kt--loadparticlevideo) memory-maps a finalized file (a gzip-compressed copy is inflated into memory
instead) and validates every lifecycle before returning a [`ParticleVideo`](video.md#particlevideo-kt-particlevideo). [`ParticleVideo.frame`](video.md#particlevideo-kt--particlevideo--frame) decodes one recorded frame;
[`ParticleVideo.at`](video.md#particlevideo-kt--particlevideo--at) scrubs by time and interpolates only between samples of the same identity.
Each [`ParticleSample`](video.md#particlevideo-kt-particlesample) carries position, velocity, sampled RGB and [`ParticleFlags`](video.md#particlevideo-kt-particleflags); each
[`ParticleTrack`](video.md#particlevideo-kt-particletrack) records one trajectory and why it was retired.

The files come from `particletracker.kt` and are drawn by `particlevideoview.kt`. Ordering,
interpolation, rejection of broken files and the compressed round trip are covered by
`ParticleVideoTest`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/media/video/particlevideo.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/media/video/particlevideo/)

**Used in:** [Video particles](../particle_video.md)

## particlevideoview.kt { #particlevideoview-kt }

Draws a loaded [`ParticleVideo`](video.md#particlevideo-kt-particlevideo) as images and as a scrubbable box output.

[`ParticleVideo.image`](video.md#particlevideoview-kt--image) rasterizes one recorded frame as per-identity trails and optional points, colored by
sampled RGB, identity or confidence. [`particleVideoView`](video.md#particlevideoview-kt--particlevideoview) puts that drawing in a box's output
with controls for movie time, colors and trails. Both work from the loaded tracks and never run
inference.

## videoFrames.kt { #videoframes-kt }

Reading a video file frame by frame as Field images, through ffmpeg.

[`videoFrames`](video.md#videoframes-kt--videoframes) is the lazy sequence of frames for a path on disk, and [`videoSize`](video.md#videoframes-kt--videosize) answers the
extent they will arrive at. ffmpeg does the decoding, the frame-rate conversion and the scaling;
[`FFMPEG`](workspace.md#doc-kt--ffmpeg) is the binary, and the ffprobe beside it reports a clip's native size. Frames arrive as
[`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img), with channel values in 0..1, so Field's imaging and sampling work on them without a
conversion step.
